authorNotes.tip: Apply the outside power to both the number and x before dividing.

distractors.A: Uses 16^(3/4) = 4 and also loses one power of x.

syllabus.primaryTopic: Algebra and functions: quadratics and discriminant

questions.stemPlain:
The line y = 2x + 3 is tangent to the curve y = x² - 4x + k.

What is the value of k?

stem.content: The line y = 2x + 3 is tangent to the curve y = x² - 4x + k.

authorNotes.solution: At an intersection, x² - 4x + k = 2x + 3, so x² - 6x + k - 3 = 0. Tangency means one repeated root, so 36 - 4(k - 3) = 0. Hence k = 12.
authorNotes.tip: For a line tangent to a quadratic, set the discriminant of the intersection equation to zero.

distractors.B: Uses the repeated x-coordinate, x = 3, as k.
distractors.C: Sets the coefficient of x, rather than the discriminant, to zero.
distractors.D: Drops k when rearranging and keeps only the line's constant term.
distractors.E: Assumes tangency occurs only when the quadratic has no constant term.

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2018 Section 1, Q77, tangent line to a quadratic; ENGAA 2021 Section 1, Q11, line-quadratic intersections.

questions.stemPlain:
The polynomial p(x) = 2x³ + ax² - 3x + 6 leaves the same remainder when divided by x - 1 and by x + 2.

What is a?

stem.content: The polynomial p(x) = 2x³ + ax² - 3x + 6 leaves the same remainder when divided by x - 1 and by x + 2.

authorNotes.solution: Equal remainders give p(1) = p(-2). Now p(1) = a + 5 and p(-2) = 4a - 4. Thus a + 5 = 4a - 4, so a = 3.
authorNotes.tip: Translate each divisor into the value to substitute before expanding anything.

distractors.A: Uses x = 2 instead of x = -2 for the divisor x + 2.
distractors.B: Changes the sign of the cubic term at x = -2 incorrectly.
distractors.C: Divides by 3 too early after forming the wrong linear equation.
distractors.D: Assumes equal remainders mean both remainders are zero.
distractors.E: Evaluates (-2)² as -4.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2023 Section 1, Q21, polynomial-factor information used to determine coefficients.

questions.stemPlain:
For x ≥ 2, let

f(x) = x² - 4x + 7    and    g(x) = √(x - 3).

Which expression is equal to g(f(x))?

authorNotes.tip: Remember that √(u²) = |u|, then use the stated domain.

distractors.A: Reverses the sign when completing the square.
distractors.B: Stops before using the restriction x ≥ 2.
distractors.D: Forgets that the outer function takes a square root.
distractors.E: Substitutes f(x) into √x rather than into √(x - 3).

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics, MM1.7 and MM8.2 composition style; no close single archive question was used.

questions.stemPlain:
Both roots of

x² - 2kx + k² - 1 = 0

are strictly between 0 and 4. Which condition on k is correct?

stem.content: \[are strictly between 0 and 4. Which condition on k is correct?\]

authorNotes.solution: The quadratic is (x - k)² = 1, so the roots are k - 1 and k + 1. Requiring 0 < k - 1 and k + 1 < 4 gives 1 < k < 3.
authorNotes.tip: Complete the square before reaching for the quadratic formula.

distractors.A: Checks only that the smaller root is below 4.
distractors.B: Checks only that the larger root is positive.
distractors.C: Uses roots -k ± 1 instead of k ± 1.
distractors.D: Applies the bounds to k itself rather than to both roots.
distractors.E: Chooses the exterior of the required interval after reversing both inequalities.
distractors.F: Includes k = 1 and k = 3, where a root equals an excluded endpoint.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2022 Section 1, Q31, complete-set inequality style; NSAA 2019 Section 1, Q89, polynomial sign intervals.

questions.stemPlain:
A sequence is defined by u₁ = 2 and uₙ₊₁ = 1 - uₙ.

What is u₂₀₂₆?

stem.content: A sequence is defined by u₁ = 2 and uₙ₊₁ = 1 - uₙ.

authorNotes.solution: The sequence alternates 2, -1, 2, -1, ... . Every even-numbered term is -1.
authorNotes.tip: Write the first three terms and look for a short cycle.

distractors.A: Changes the sign but forgets the added 1.
distractors.C: Treats the recurrence as uₙ₊₁ = 1 - n.
distractors.D: Uses the value of the odd-numbered terms.

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics, MM2.1 recurrence exercises; broader ESAT sequence style.

questions.stemPlain:
An arithmetic progression has first term a, non-zero common difference d, and sum Sₙ of its first n terms.

Given that S₁₀ = 3S₅, what is a/d?

stem.content: An arithmetic progression has first term a, non-zero common difference d, and sum Sₙ of its first n terms.

authorNotes.solution: S₁₀ = 5(2a + 9d) and S₅ = (5/2)(2a + 4d). Setting S₁₀ = 3S₅ gives 10(2a + 9d) = 15(2a + 4d), so a = 3d.
authorNotes.tip: Cancel the common factor 5 before doing the algebra.

distractors.A: Moves the d terms across with the wrong sign.
distractors.B: Uses 10d and 5d instead of 9d and 4d in the sum formula.
distractors.C: Cancels a from both sides even though it is inside brackets.
distractors.D: Uses Sₙ = n(a + d)/2.
distractors.F: Equates the tenth term to three times the fifth term instead of the sums.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2023 Section 1, Q23, linked arithmetic sums; NSAA 2018 Section 1, Q79, conditions on an arithmetic progression.

questions.stemPlain:
What is the coefficient of x² in

(1 - 2x)⁵ + (1 + 2x)⁵?

stem.content: What is the coefficient of x² in

authorNotes.solution: Each expansion contributes C(5,2)(2x)² = 10 × 4x² = 40x². The signs are positive for an even power, so the total coefficient is 80.
authorNotes.tip: Odd-power terms cancel, but even-power terms add.

distractors.A: Assumes every non-constant term cancels.
distractors.B: Finds the coefficient from only one expansion.
distractors.D: Adds the two contributions and then doubles once more.
distractors.E: Uses 2⁵ instead of 2² for the x² term.

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2018 Section 1, Q85, coefficient extraction with paired binomial factors.

questions.stemPlain:
The line through A(1, 4) and B(5, 2) is perpendicular to line L. Line L passes through A.

What is the equation of L?

stem.content: The line through A(1, 4) and B(5, 2) is perpendicular to line L. Line L passes through A.

authorNotes.solution: The gradient of AB is (2 - 4)/(5 - 1) = -1/2, so the perpendicular gradient is 2. Through A, y - 4 = 2(x - 1), hence y = 2x + 2.
authorNotes.tip: Find the gradient first, then use the negative reciprocal.

distractors.B: Uses the correct gradient but substitutes A incorrectly.
distractors.C: Changes the sign of the gradient but does not take the reciprocal.
distractors.D: Uses the equation of AB itself.
distractors.E: Takes the reciprocal but keeps the negative sign.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2018 Section 1, Q5, parallel-gradient reasoning; ENGAA 2022 Section 1, Q37, point-to-line geometry.

questions.stemPlain:
The circle (x - 2)² + (y + 1)² = 9 has centre C. A tangent from P(8, -1) touches the circle at T, as shown.

What is PT?

stem.content: The circle (x - 2)² + (y + 1)² = 9 has centre C. A tangent from P(8, -1) touches the circle at T, as shown.

diagram.alt: Coordinate diagram of a circle centred at C(2,-1), an external point P(8,-1), and tangent PT.

authorNotes.solution: CP = 6 and CT = 3. Since CT is perpendicular to the tangent, triangle CTP is right-angled. Thus PT² = 6² - 3² = 27, so PT = 3√3.
authorNotes.tip: Join the external point to the centre to create a right-angled triangle.

distractors.A: Uses the difference of the two lengths and then halves it.
distractors.B: Calculates √(6 - 3) instead of using squares.
distractors.C: Assumes the tangent length equals the radius.
distractors.D: Uses PT² = CP × CT.
distractors.E: Uses PT² = CP² - CT rather than CP² - CT².

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2018 Section 1, Q83, tangent length from an external point to a circle.

syllabus.primaryTopic: Coordinate geometry: equation of a circle

questions.stemPlain:
The points A(-1, 2) and B(5, 6) are the endpoints of a diameter of a circle.

Which is the equation of the circle?

stem.content: The points A(-1, 2) and B(5, 6) are the endpoints of a diameter of a circle.
\[Which is the equation of the circle?\]

authorNotes.solution: The centre is the midpoint (2, 4). Also AB² = 6² + 4² = 52, so r² = AB²/4 = 13. Therefore (x - 2)² + (y - 4)² = 13.
authorNotes.tip: The diameter is twice the radius, so square lengths with care.

distractors.A: Uses the squared diameter as r².
distractors.B: Uses the right radius but reverses both centre signs.
distractors.C: Divides the squared diameter by 2 instead of 4.
distractors.E: Finds the wrong midpoint by pairing unlike coordinates.

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics, MM3.2 circle-equation examples; broader coordinate-geometry style in ENGAA 2022 Q37.

questions.stemPlain:
Evaluate

(sin 30° + cos 60°) / tan 45°.

authorNotes.solution: sin 30° = cos 60° = 1/2 and tan 45° = 1. The value is (1/2 + 1/2)/1 = 1.
authorNotes.tip: Recall the exact values before doing any manipulation.

distractors.A: Uses only one term in the numerator.
distractors.C: Confuses sin 45° with tan 45°.
distractors.D: Divides each half by 1/2 instead of by 1.
distractors.E: Uses tan 45° = 1/√2 and also doubles the numerator.

authorNotes.calibration: Official Pearson ESAT Mathematics 2 specimen, exact-trigonometric-value style; specification MM4.3.

questions.stemPlain:
A circle has radius 6. A minor arc AB has length 4π, and the minor segment cut off by chord AB is shaded.

What is the exact area of the shaded segment?

stem.content: A circle has radius 6. A minor arc AB has length 4π, and the minor segment cut off by chord AB is shaded.
\[What is the exact area of the shaded segment?\]

diagram.alt: Circle sector with central angle two pi over three and the minor segment shaded.

authorNotes.solution: The angle is θ = s/r = 4π/6 = 2π/3. Sector area is (1/2)r²θ = 12π. Triangle AOB has area (1/2)(6)(6)sin(2π/3) = 9√3. The segment area is 12π - 9√3.
authorNotes.tip: A segment is a sector minus the triangle formed by the two radii.

distractors.A: Uses the arc length as if it were the angle.
distractors.B: Uses θ = π/3 rather than 2π/3.
distractors.C: Uses πrθ/2 for the sector area.
distractors.D: Forgets the factor 1/2 in the triangle area.
distractors.E: Adds the triangle instead of subtracting it.
distractors.F: Uses the whole 18π half-circle area as the sector.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2021 Section 1, Q27, exact area of a circular segment; official specification MM4.2.

questions.stemPlain:
How many solutions of

2sin²x + cos x = 3/2

lie in 0 ≤ x < 2π?

authorNotes.solution: Let c = cos x and use sin²x = 1 - c². This gives 4c² - 2c - 1 = 0, with roots c = (1 ± √5)/4. Both lie strictly between -1 and 1, so each cosine value gives two x-values in the interval. Total: 4.
authorNotes.tip: You only need to check whether the cosine roots lie in [-1, 1]; you do not need their angles.

distractors.A: Rejects the irrational cosine values because they are not standard angles.
distractors.B: Keeps only one root of the quadratic and one angle.
distractors.C: Keeps both cosine roots but gives one angle for each.
distractors.D: Treats one valid cosine root as an endpoint value with only one angle.

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2018 Section 1, Q75, counting trigonometric solutions in a radian interval.

questions.stemPlain:
An acute angle θ satisfies tan θ = 3/4.

What is sin θ - cos θ?

stem.content: An acute angle θ satisfies tan θ = 3/4.

authorNotes.solution: Use a 3-4-5 triangle. Then sin θ = 3/5 and cos θ = 4/5, so sin θ - cos θ = -1/5.
authorNotes.tip: Turn a positive tangent ratio into a right triangle.

distractors.A: Subtracts 4 from 3 without dividing by the hypotenuse.
distractors.B: Uses sin θ = 0.
distractors.D: Reverses the order of subtraction.
distractors.E: Adds sine and cosine instead of subtracting.

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2019 Section 1, Q77, reducing a trigonometric condition to algebraic ratios.

authorNotes.solution: Write both sides in base 2: 2^(2x - 2) = 2^(3x + 3). Hence 2x - 2 = 3x + 3, giving x = -5.
authorNotes.tip: Convert both sides to the same base before comparing exponents.

distractors.B: Drops the factor 2 multiplying x - 1.
distractors.C: Equates x - 1 and x + 1 directly.
distractors.D: Changes 8 to 2² instead of 2³.
distractors.E: Moves the constants across with the wrong sign.

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2019 Section 1, Q81, exponential equation reduced using a substitution or common base.

questions.stemPlain:
Evaluate

log₂(3/2) + log₂(4/3) + log₂(5/4) + ... + log₂(32/31).

authorNotes.solution: Combine the logarithms. The product telescopes to (3/2)(4/3)...(32/31) = 32/2 = 16. Therefore the sum is log₂16 = 4.
authorNotes.tip: Combine first, then cancel the product before evaluating the logarithm.

distractors.A: Reverses every fraction before combining.
distractors.B: Keeps only the first and last denominators in the wrong order.
distractors.C: Assumes a telescoping product must equal the base 2.
distractors.E: Uses 32 = 2⁵ and forgets the remaining division by 2.

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2018 Section 1, Q81, telescoping sum of logarithms.

questions.stemPlain:
Two quantities are modelled by

P = 3 × 2ᵗ    and    Q = 96 × 2^(-t).

For what value of t are P and Q equal?

stem.content: \[For what value of t are P and Q equal?\]

authorNotes.solution: Set the models equal: 3 × 2ᵗ = 96 × 2^(-t). Hence 2^(2t) = 32 = 2⁵, so 2t = 5 and t = 5/2.
authorNotes.tip: Bring equal bases together before comparing exponents.

distractors.A: Moves 2^(-t) across but keeps the exponent negative.
distractors.C: Assumes the increasing and decreasing models meet at t = 0.
distractors.D: Uses 32 = 2².
distractors.E: Finds 2t = 4 after treating 32 as 16.

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics, MM5.3 exponential-equation modelling; broader ESAT intersection style.

questions.stemPlain:
The curve y = x³ - 3x has a normal at the point where x = 2.

Which is the equation of the normal?

stem.content: The curve y = x³ - 3x has a normal at the point where x = 2.
\[Which is the equation of the normal?\]

diagram.alt: Graph of y equals x cubed minus 3x with tangent and normal at (2,2).

authorNotes.solution: At x = 2, y = 2. Also dy/dx = 3x² - 3, so the tangent gradient is 9 and the normal gradient is -1/9. Thus y - 2 = -(x - 2)/9.
authorNotes.tip: Find both the point and the negative reciprocal gradient.

distractors.A: Uses the tangent gradient instead of the normal gradient.
distractors.C: Uses (-2, -2) instead of (2, 2).
distractors.D: Differentiates x³ as 3x instead of 3x².
distractors.E: Takes the reciprocal but forgets the negative sign.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2021 Section 1, Q21, efficient derivative evaluation; official MM6.3 tangent and normal style.

questions.stemPlain:
For a > 0, the curve

y = x³ - 3ax + 2

has a stationary point on the x-axis. What is a?

stem.content: \[has a stationary point on the x-axis. What is a?\]

authorNotes.solution: At a stationary point, 3x² - 3a = 0, so a = x². Being on the x-axis also gives x³ - 3x³ + 2 = 0, hence x³ = 1. Therefore x = 1 and a = 1.
authorNotes.tip: Use the derivative equation to remove the parameter from the curve equation.

distractors.A: Uses a = -x² and x = 2.
distractors.B: Substitutes x³ = 2 instead of x³ = 1.
distractors.C: Takes x = -1 even though it does not make the point lie on the axis.
distractors.D: Assumes a stationary point on an axis must occur at the origin.
distractors.F: Uses x³ = 2 after missing the factor -2x³.
distractors.G: Squares the constant term 2 to obtain a.

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics, MM6.3 stationary-point parameter exercises; tangent condition style also seen in NSAA 2018 Q77.

questions.stemPlain:
An open box is made from a 12 by 8 rectangular sheet by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides.

For 0 < x < 4, which value of x gives the maximum volume?

stem.content: An open box is made from a 12 by 8 rectangular sheet by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides.
\[For 0 < x < 4, which value of x gives the maximum volume?\]

diagram.alt: Twelve by eight rectangular sheet with four corner squares of side x marked for removal.

authorNotes.solution: V = x(12 - 2x)(8 - 2x) = 4x(6 - x)(4 - x). Differentiating gives V' = 12x² - 80x + 96. Thus 3x² - 20x + 24 = 0, so x = (10 ± 2√7)/3. Only the minus sign lies in 0 < x < 4, so it gives the maximum.
authorNotes.tip: Use the physical interval to reject the second stationary value immediately.

distractors.A: Keeps the stationary value outside the physical domain.
distractors.B: Loses the factor 2 when applying the quadratic formula.
distractors.C: Uses 8 rather than 10 in the quadratic-formula numerator.
distractors.D: Differentiates the three factors separately but does not use the product rule correctly.
distractors.E: Keeps only the square-root part of the solution.
distractors.F: Assumes the best cut is half the smaller side's half-width.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2022 Section 1, Q23, forming an area model from a diagram; official 2026 Notes MM6.3 optimisation style.

questions.stemPlain:
The line y = x - 1 is shown for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3. The two regions between the line and the x-axis are shaded.

What is the total shaded area?

stem.content: The line y = x - 1 is shown for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3. The two regions between the line and the x-axis are shaded.

diagram.alt: Graph of y equals x minus 1 from x equals zero to three with both regions to the x-axis shaded.

authorNotes.solution: From 0 to 1 the triangle has area 1/2. From 1 to 3 the triangle has area (1/2)(2)(2) = 2. Total area = 1/2 + 2 = 5/2.
authorNotes.tip: Areas below the axis still count positively in a total geometric area.

distractors.A: Calculates the signed integral, 2 - 1/2.
distractors.B: Counts only the region above the axis.
distractors.D: Adds the two triangle bases but omits the factor 1/2.
distractors.E: Treats the smaller triangle as having area 3/2.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2018 Section 1, Q29, area enclosed by a curve and a line; official MM7.1 signed-area distinction.

questions.stemPlain:
The area under y = x² from x = 0 to x = 2 is estimated using the trapezium rule with ordinates at x = 0, 1 and 2.

Which row is correct?

stem.content: The area under y = x² from x = 0 to x = 2 is estimated using the trapezium rule with ordinates at x = 0, 1 and 2.

diagram.alt: Graph of y equals x squared with two trapezia on intervals zero to one and one to two.

authorNotes.solution: With width 1, the trapezium estimate is (1/2)[0 + 2(1) + 4] = 3. Since y = x² is convex, the chords lie above the curve, so this is an overestimate.
authorNotes.tip: For a convex curve, trapezium tops sit above the curve.

distractors.B: Gets the numerical estimate right but reverses the convexity judgement.
distractors.C: Uses the exact integral instead of the trapezium estimate.
distractors.D: Uses the midpoint value as an average height.
distractors.E: Adds the three ordinates without endpoint half-weights.

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics, MM7.5 trapezium-rule and overestimate style; no close archive item was used.

questions.stemPlain:
A curve satisfies dy/dx = 6x - 4 and passes through (1, 5).

What is the value of y when x = 2?

stem.content: A curve satisfies dy/dx = 6x - 4 and passes through (1, 5).
\[What is the value of y when x = 2?\]

authorNotes.solution: Integrating gives y = 3x² - 4x + C. Using (1, 5), 5 = 3 - 4 + C, so C = 6. At x = 2, y = 12 - 8 + 6 = 10.
authorNotes.tip: Find the constant before substituting the requested x-value.

distractors.A: Assumes the initial y-value remains constant.
distractors.B: Finds C correctly but reports it as the answer.
distractors.C: Integrates 6x as 3x rather than 3x².
distractors.D: Omits the constant of integration.
distractors.E: Uses C = 5 without applying the point to the other terms.

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics, MM7.6 first-order differential-equation examples.

questions.stemPlain:
The graph of y = f(x) has a maximum at (-2, 3) and x-intercepts at (-4, 0) and (0, 0), as shown.

What is the turning point of y = -2f(x + 1) + 5?

stem.content: The graph of y = f(x) has a maximum at (-2, 3) and x-intercepts at (-4, 0) and (0, 0), as shown.
\[What is the turning point of y = -2f(x + 1) + 5?\]

diagram.alt: Downward parabola with roots (-4,0) and (0,0) and maximum (-2,3).

authorNotes.solution: Replacing x by x + 1 shifts the graph left by 1, so the x-coordinate becomes -3. The y-value transforms as -2(3) + 5 = -1. The turning point is (-3, -1).
authorNotes.tip: Do the horizontal transformation first, and remember its direction is reversed.

distractors.A: Shifts the graph right instead of left.
distractors.B: Shifts left but uses 2(3) + 5.
distractors.C: Shifts right and also misses the reflection.
distractors.E: Changes the sign of the original x-coordinate instead of shifting it.

authorNotes.calibration: Official Pearson ESAT Mathematics 2 specimen and 2026 Notes MM8.2 graph-transformation style.

questions.stemPlain:
How many distinct real solutions does

x³ - 3x = 2

have?

stem.content: How many distinct real solutions does

diagram.alt: Graph of y equals x cubed minus 3x and horizontal line y equals 2, tangent at x equals -1 and crossing at x equals 2.

authorNotes.solution: Rearrange to x³ - 3x - 2 = 0. This factorises as (x - 2)(x + 1)² = 0, giving the two distinct roots x = 2 and x = -1. The repeated root represents tangency to y = 2.
authorNotes.tip: The question asks for distinct roots, so inspect multiplicity after factorising.

distractors.A: Counts only the crossing at x = 2 and misses the tangent root.
distractors.C: Counts the repeated root x = -1 twice.
distractors.D: Assumes a cubic and a line can meet in four places.

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2018 Section 1, Q77, tangency as a repeated algebraic solution; ENGAA 2021 Section 1, Q11, intersections encoded by a quadratic.

questions.stemPlain:
The graph shown is decreasing, has horizontal asymptote y = -3, and passes through (0, -1).

Which is its equation?

stem.content: The graph shown is decreasing, has horizontal asymptote y = -3, and passes through (0, -1).

diagram.alt: Decreasing exponential through (0,-1) with horizontal asymptote y equals -3.

authorNotes.solution: A decreasing base-2 exponential needs a negative coefficient of x in the exponent. The asymptote -3 fixes the vertical shift. At x = 0, 2^(1 - 0) - 3 = -1, so y = 2^(1 - x) - 3.
authorNotes.tip: Use the asymptote and direction first, then check one point.

distractors.A: Has the right asymptote but is increasing and has y-intercept -2.
distractors.B: Is decreasing but has asymptote y = 3.
distractors.C: Has the right intercept and asymptote but is increasing.
distractors.D: Is decreasing and has the right intercept, but its asymptote is y = -1.

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics, MM5.1 and MM8.1-2 exponential-graph style; official Pearson specimen graph interpretation.

authorNotes.solution: The common denominator is (√5 - 2)(√5 + 2) = 1. The numerator is (√5 + 2) - (√5 - 2) = 4, so the value is 4.
authorNotes.tip: Conjugate denominators often collapse to a small integer.

distractors.A: Subtracts the two 2s instead of accounting for the outer minus sign.
distractors.C: Adds the surd parts and cancels the rational parts.
distractors.D: Uses 5 + 4 as the denominator rather than the difference of squares.
distractors.E: Doubles the numerator again after rationalising both fractions.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2022 Section 1, Q27, exact simplification of a surd expression.

questions.stemPlain:
The line y = x + 2 intersects the curve y = x² - k at two points. The difference between their x-coordinates is 4.

What is k?

stem.content: The line y = x + 2 intersects the curve y = x² - k at two points. The difference between their x-coordinates is 4.

authorNotes.solution: Intersections satisfy x² - x - (k + 2) = 0. For a monic quadratic, the root difference has square equal to the discriminant: 1 + 4(k + 2) = 4k + 9. Hence 4k + 9 = 16 and k = 7/4.
authorNotes.tip: For roots r and s of a monic quadratic, (r - s)² equals the discriminant.

distractors.A: Moves 9 across with the wrong sign.
distractors.B: Uses the difference 4 as the discriminant rather than 4².
distractors.C: Drops the +2 when equating the graphs.
distractors.D: Uses 4k + 1 for the discriminant.

authorNotes.calibration: ENGAA 2021 Section 1, Q11, deducing a line-curve parameter from the separation of intersection roots.

questions.stemPlain:
The polynomial x² + x - 6 is a factor of

x³ + ax² + bx + 12.

What is a + b?

stem.content: The polynomial x² + x - 6 is a factor of

authorNotes.solution: Since x² + x - 6 = (x + 3)(x - 2), the remaining factor is x + c. The constant term is -6c = 12, so c = -2. Expanding (x² + x - 6)(x - 2) gives a = -1 and b = -8, hence a + b = -9.
authorNotes.tip: Use the constant term to find the linear quotient before expanding.

distractors.B: Reports the constant coefficient of the quadratic factor.
distractors.C: Uses c = 2 instead of c = -2.

questions.stemPlain:
In a triangle, two sides of lengths 4 and 5 enclose angle θ. The side opposite θ has length 3.

What is cos θ?

stem.content: In a triangle, two sides of lengths 4 and 5 enclose angle θ. The side opposite θ has length 3.

diagram.alt: Right triangle with side lengths three, four and five, with angle theta between sides four and five.

authorNotes.solution: By the cosine rule, 3² = 4² + 5² - 2(4)(5)cos θ. Thus 9 = 41 - 40cos θ, so cos θ = 32/40 = 4/5.
authorNotes.tip: The side opposite the angle is the one that appears alone on the left of the cosine rule.

distractors.A: Uses the smallest side divided by the largest as the cosine.
distractors.B: Uses 16/40 after omitting 5².

questions.stemPlain:
A triangle ABC satisfies A = 30°, a = 4 and b = 6, where side a is opposite A and side b is opposite B.

How many different triangles satisfy these data?

stem.content: A triangle ABC satisfies A = 30°, a = 4 and b = 6, where side a is opposite A and side b is opposite B.
\[How many different triangles satisfy these data?\]

authorNotes.solution: The sine rule gives sin B = b sin A/a = 6(1/2)/4 = 3/4. There is an acute value B and its obtuse supplement. Since the acute B is greater than 30°, its supplement still leaves A + B < 180°. Both triangles are valid.
authorNotes.tip: In an angle-side-side problem, check both B and 180° - B.

distractors.A: Treats b > a as impossible even though B is also larger than A.
distractors.B: Keeps only the principal acute value of B.
distractors.D: Counts the acute angle, its supplement and a reflected drawing as three different triangles.

authorNotes.calibration: Official 2026 Notes on Mathematics and specification MM4.1, which explicitly includes the ambiguous sine-rule case.

questions.stemPlain:
How many solutions of

tan x (tan²x - 1) = 0

lie in 0 ≤ x ≤ 2π?

authorNotes.solution: Either tan x = 0 or tan x = ±1. In the closed interval, tan x = 0 at 0, π and 2π, giving three solutions. The equations tan x = 1 and tan x = -1 give two each, for four more. The undefined points π/2 and 3π/2 are not solutions. Total: 7.
authorNotes.tip: Count endpoints carefully and exclude the vertical asymptotes of tan x.

distractors.A: Counts only the factor tan x = 0 at x = 0.
distractors.B: Counts only the two tan x = 1 solutions.
distractors.C: Counts tan x = 0 but omits both ±1 branches.
distractors.D: Counts the ±1 branches but omits tan x = 0.
distractors.E: Counts two zeros of tan and the four ±1 solutions, then loses one branch.
distractors.F: Omits one of the equal endpoints 0 or 2π.

authorNotes.calibration: NSAA 2018 Section 1, Q75, counting all trigonometric solutions in a specified interval.

authorNotes.solution: The arc length is 12 - 2(3) = 6, so the angle is θ = 6/3 = 2 radians. The sector area is (1/2)(3²)(2) = 9. The triangle area is (1/2)(3²)sin 2 = (9/2)sin 2. Subtracting gives 9 - (9/2)sin 2.
authorNotes.tip: Use the perimeter to find the arc length before finding the angle.

questions.stemPlain:
The curve y = (3/2)x(x - 1) is shown from x = 0 to x = 2. The regions between the curve and the x-axis are shaded.

What is the total shaded area?

stem.content: The curve y = (3/2)x(x - 1) is shown from x = 0 to x = 2. The regions between the curve and the x-axis are shaded.

diagram.alt: Graph of y equals three halves x times x minus one from zero to two, with both axis regions shaded.

authorNotes.solution: An antiderivative is F(x) = x³/2 - 3x²/4. From 0 to 1, the integral is -1/4, so that area is 1/4. From 1 to 2, the integral is F(2) - F(1) = 1 - (-1/4) = 5/4. The total area is 1/4 + 5/4 = 3/2.
authorNotes.tip: Split at every x-intercept and make each geometric contribution positive.

distractors.A: Uses only F(2), the signed integral from 0 to 2.
distractors.C: Adds the magnitudes but doubles the smaller region.
distractors.D: Adds 5/4 and 5/4, treating the two regions as equal.
